note: After Ruelle 1970 (pp. 419—424; neotype alate, major soldier, minor soldier, major worker). The original is in English. Some values in the tables are missing from the scanned text layer (of the measurement tables for the major soldier and the alate only the row labels survive), so only the readable measurements are retained: the complete set of values for the minor soldier is intact, while for the alate and the worker the regional ranges given in the running-text section on variation are used. The original uses hyphens in place of decimal points (e.g. 2-67-4-45, i.e. 2.67—4.45) and these have been converted. Nomenclatural point: the name 'bellicosus' in the literature since Hagen 1858 mostly refers to this species; Ruelle held that all 'bellicosus' records from the range of this species that were not included in his revision should be assigned to it.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate head chestnut brown, the vertex in lateral view evenly convex and not humped (contrary to M. bellicosus); around the fontanelle there is a distinct semicircular depressed area in dorsal view, the fontanelle itself projecting and surrounded by short hairs, with a narrow median ridge running forwards from it to the anteclypeus. Major soldier: head thicker in lateral view, the frons more or less truncate, the left mandible almost as long as the head depth; pronotum large, its length more than half its width, the anterior and posterior margins equally concave, the lateral corners rounded.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head chestnut brown; anteclypeus paler than the head, with a fine and inconspicuous dark median line. Pronotum concolorous with the head, with a pale T-shaped mark in the middle and two pale dots near the anterior lateral corners; abdominal tergites concolorous with the pronotum, the sternites paler. Legs with less red than the head, the tibiae slightly darker than the femora; wings yellowish brown. Head in dorsal view with a distinct semicircular depression around the fontanelle; fontanelle projecting, surrounded by short hairs, with a narrow median ridge running forwards from it to the anteclypeus; vertex in lateral view evenly convex, not humped (contrary to M. bellicosus). Compound eyes large, not very projecting, round; ocelli slightly elongate, their distance from the compound eyes about a fraction of their long diameter (the original fraction is illegible in the scan and is therefore not entered). Anteclypeus moderately swollen. Antennae 19-segmented, segment 3 the longest, segment 2 as long as segment 4. Anterior margin of the pronotum convex, the posterior margin slightly concave, the anterior lateral corners pointed. Body size varies regionally: in West Africa the alate head width (across the compound eyes) is 3.15—3.45 mm, in East Africa 3.30—3.87 mm, Central Africa being intermediate; fore wing length 35.0—40.0 mm in Central Africa, 30.0—43.0 mm in East Africa (the upper limit being exceptional), 29.0—35.0 mm in West Africa.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: head red-yellow to red-brown, usually paler below, the sides of the postmentum darker than the cheeks below; antennae darker than the head capsule; mandibles black with red at the base. Thoracic tergites dark brown at the margins, yellowish brown in the middle; the rest of the body concolorous with the thorax, but the abdominal sternites paler than the tergites and the tibiae darker than the femora. Head rectangular in dorsal view, slightly narrowing forwards, with 1 groove on each side from the fontanelle to the mandibular articulation; thicker in lateral view, the frons more or less truncate. Mandibles stout, the left slightly wider and more incurved, almost as long as the head depth; setae sparse, slightly denser on the postmentum; the transparent apex of the labrum usually convex on both sides. Antennae 17-segmented, segment 3 about twice as long as segment 2. Pronotum large, its length more than half its width, the anterior and posterior margins equally concave, the lateral corners rounded, the setae longer than those of the head capsule; mesonotum slightly narrower than the pronotum; metanotum in most specimens narrower than the mesonotum, the posterior margin flat to concave; all 3 tergites strongly sclerotized. Minor soldier: head yellowish brown to chestnut brown, paler than in the major soldier; the anterior outline deeper, especially between the antennal sockets and the mandibular condyles; postmentum darker than the cheeks. Mandibles black with dark red at the base; antennae smoky brown, darker than the head capsule. Thorax darker or paler than the head capsule, the tergite outline mostly darker than the middle; abdominal sternites concolorous with the tergites and paler than the thorax; femora and tibiae of the abdominal colour (the tibiae often darker), the tarsi darker. Head quadrate-oblong in dorsal view, the sides nearly straight; fontanelle usually distinct and sometimes projecting, with a weak median ridge in front of it; mandibles slender, incurved and slightly upturned; head capsule with very sparse setae, the labrum and the body with slightly more, the setae darker than the cuticle. Inner margin of the left mandible without teeth. Sides of the pronotum rather straight from the rounded anterior lateral corners to the posterior margin, the anterior and posterior margins both concave; sides of the meso- and metanotum rounded, the metanotum slightly wider than the mesonotum. Measurements (439 specimens, 146 localities): head length 2.67—4.45 (mean 3.57) mm, head width 2.31—3.55 (mean 2.87) mm, head depth including the postmentum 1.52—2.24 (mean 1.87) mm, postmentum length 1.81—2.66 (mean 2.32) mm, postmentum maximum width 0.81—1.01 (mean 0.92) mm, left mandible length 1.85—2.90 (mean 2.41) mm, hind tibia length 2.19—3.35 (mean 2.78) mm, maximum length of the pronotum 1.04—1.55 (mean 1.33) mm, maximum width of the pronotum 1.86—2.75 (mean 2.36) mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Major worker head deep chestnut brown; in dorsal view the sides slightly convex, the posterior margin rounded. Head width 2.18—3.27 mm, mean 2.75 mm (335 specimens, 114 localities).
